key_insight: DMA² shows that distribution matching distillation works differently in pixel-space than in latent space: low-noise RGB matching is overly driven by local texture, so the paper shifts matching to a fixed high-noise band and adds anchor-based guidance for better few-step generation.
problem_solved: The paper addresses how to adapt distribution matching distillation for native RGB diffusion models, where standard latent-space assumptions miss important pixel-space behavior and can lead to poor training signals.
method: Analyze teacher-matching behavior in pixel-space and identify that low-noise matching is dominated by local texture cues.
Use a fixed high-noise matching band to provide more meaningful distribution-matching supervision.
Introduce adversarial and anchor losses to stabilize training and preserve fidelity while improving few-step generation.
impact: This work gives practitioners a more effective recipe for few-step RGB image generation without relying on latent diffusion. It opens a path to faster, native-pixel text-to-image models with better training stability and more faithful outputs.

paper_title: DMA$^2$: Pixel-space Distribution Matching with Adversarial and Anchor Losses
